blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) requires agents to diagnose system bottlenecks and coordinate improvements across training and inference. We refer to the agents' capability to jointly optimize training data, the trainer, and the inference harness as cross-component co-design. We introduce VibeTraining-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating this capability across tasks spanning terminal operation, software engineering, multi-turn tool use, and mathematical reasoning. Within each task, research agents start from an identical initial agent system under a fixed resource budget. Guided by validation feedback, they iteratively refine data, trainers, and inference harnesses, then select and submit a final agent system for evaluation on the test set. To prevent reward hacking, we enforce three safeguards: test data isolation, separate research and grading containers, and network restrictions for research agents. Our evaluation results show that frontier research agents substantially improve target agent systems. For example, on SWE-bench Verified, GPT-6-Astra raises the target agent system's performance from 32.9% to 53.7%, comparable to the human-developed instruct model's 55.4%. However, there is still room to improve their ability to co-design and iteratively refine data, trainer, and harness to achieve cumulative performance gains. We hope that VibeTraining-Bench will serve as a unified platform for advancing RSI, deepening our understanding of cross-component optimization for agent systems. Code and data are available at https://github.com/D2I-ai/VibeTrainingBench.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Recursive self-improvement (RSI), increasingly studied as a path toward autonomous AI development, requires agents to diagnose performance bottlenecks and propose and validate modifications to an agent system ( Liu et al., 2026 ; Yang et al., 2026 ) . These modifications may involve training data, the trainer, and the inference harness, with their effectiveness depending on how these components are configured together ( Ursekar et al., 2026 ) . For example, the harness controls what an agent observes and can do, steering its exploration and thus the trajectories the model learns from; conversely, the model’s capabilities determine what the harness must provide ( Chen et al., 2026a ; Chen et al., 2026d ) . Agents must therefore trace failures to their sources and coordinate changes across training and inference. We refer to this capability as cross-component co-design .
blocks.zh: 递归自我改进(RSI),作为自主AI开发的途径日益被研究,要求代理商诊断性能瓶颈,提出并验证对代理系统的修改(刘等人,2026年;杨等人,2026年). 这些修改可能涉及培训数据、训练员和推断手段,其有效性取决于这些组件如何组合在一起(Ursekar等人,2026年)。 例如,绳索控制着一种物剂所观察到的和能够做的,指导着它的探索,从而控制着模型从中吸取的轨迹;相反,绳索的能力决定着它必须提供什么(Chen等人,2026a; 陈等, 2026d ). 因此,代理人必须追踪其来源的失败情况,并协调各种培训和推论的变化。 我们把这种能力称为交叉组件共同设计。

blocks.en:
Assessing cross-component co-design thus calls for settings in which agents themselves determine which components to modify and how to coordinate these modifications as the system evolves. To the best of our knowledge, few benchmarks directly assess this capability.
MLE-Bench and RE-Bench evaluate research agents on diverse machine learning engineering and research tasks, focusing on task-specific research outcomes. More directly related RSI benchmarks often evaluate single-component improvement. RSIBench-Data ( Meng et al., 2026 ) , AI4AI-Bench ( Chi et al., 2026 ) , and HarnessOpt-Bench ( Ursekar et al., 2026 ) focus on data strategies, training algorithms, and inference harnesses, respectively; each MLS-Bench task specifies one ML component to improve ( Lyu et al., 2026 ) . These benchmarks evaluate improvements within predefined
component scopes. PostTrainBench ( Rank et al., 2026 ) and Agent 2 RL-Bench ( Chen et al., 2026c ) broaden this scope to data construction and post-training procedures. Simply broadening the editable scope also raises evaluation risks: PostTrainBench reports reward hacking, including research agents training on test data ( Rank et al., 2026 ) . Even these multi-component benchmarks remain focused on
training-side optimization, leaving the iterative selection
and coordination of changes across training and inference
within the same evolving target system unexplored.

blocks.en:
We introduce VibeTraining-Bench to evaluate cross-component co-design through five tasks spanning terminal operation, software engineering, multi-turn tool use, and mathematical reasoning.
In each task, an agent receives an initial agent system comprising a base model, open-source training data, a trainer with algorithm code and initial scripts, and an inference harness. The agent must improve this system within a fixed resource budget, and the agent it finally submits is then scored on hidden test instances.
During a run, validation scores and execution trajectories help the agent trace failures to their sources and assess successive revisions. The benchmark also allows the agent to choose where to intervene and coordinate changes across components. Training data and the trainer are editable in every task, as is the inference harness unless the task’s evaluation prescribes a particular harness.
These design choices, however, also widen the opportunities for reward hacking, so VibeTraining-Bench further enforces three safeguards, namely data isolation, container isolation, and network restrictions. Specifically, test data remain inaccessible throughout the research phase; research and grading run in separate containers, preventing research agents from modifying grader code or evaluation data; and research environments strictly restrict external network access.
blocks.zh:
我们引入了VibeTraining-Bench,通过跨越终端操作,软件工程,多回合工具使用和数学推理的五个任务来评价跨组件共同设计.
在每项任务中,一个代理接收一个初始代理系统,包括一个基础模型,开源培训数据,一个具备算法代码和初始脚本的教练员,以及一个推论机. 代理商必须在固定的资源预算范围内改进这个系统,它最后提交的代理商然后在隐藏的测试实例上得分.
在运行中,验证分数和执行轨迹帮助代理追踪故障源头并评估连续的修订. 该基准还允许代理人选择干预和协调各组成部分变化的地点。 在每项任务中,培训数据和培训人员都可以编辑,推论的利用也一样,除非任务评价规定了一种特定的利用方式。
然而,这些设计选择也拓宽了奖励黑客的机会,因此VibeTraining-Bench进一步实施三项保障措施,即数据隔离,集装箱隔离,和网络限制. 具体地说,测试数据在整个研究阶段始终无法获取;研究和分级分解在单独的容器中运行,使研究代理人无法修改分级编码或评价数据;研究环境严格限制外部网络访问.

blocks.en:
Our evaluation results show that frontier research agents substantially improve target agent systems.
For example, on SWE-bench Verified, GPT-6-Astra coordinates training and harness changes, raising the target agent system’s performance from 32.9% to 53.7%, comparable to the human-developed instruct model’s 55.4%. However, research agents explore the improvable system components unevenly. Analysis of research trajectories shows that agents primarily focus on lightweight refinements, such as data filtering and training hyperparameter tuning. They less frequently explore changes to the underlying training algorithms or coordinated modifications across training data, the trainer, and the inference harness.
There is still room for improvement in research agents’ cross-component co-design capability and iterative refinement toward achieving cumulative performance gains.

研究代理商的跨组成部分共同设计能力仍有改进余地,并不断改进,以实现累积业绩收益。

blocks.en:
In summary, we make the following contributions: • We introduce VibeTraining-Bench , a benchmark spanning diverse tasks for evaluating cross-component co-design of target agent systems. Its improvement scope encompasses training data, the trainer, and the inference harness. • We develop a reliable execution platform to guarantee evaluation integrity. To prevent research agents from reward hacking, our platform implements three levels of safeguards by isolating test data, separating research and grading containers, and restricting external network access. • We evaluate frontier research agents through test performance, research trajectories, and component ablations. Research agents substantially improve target agent systems, in some cases approaching the performance of the system with human post-training.
Our experimental analysis reveals that research agents built upon frontier models and harnesses still exhibit limitations on these tasks, indicating substantial room for further improvement.

blocks.en:
Self-improving agent systems expose several non-exclusive intervention surfaces: training data, trainer, and inference-time harnesses.
On the data front, prior work improves models through automated experience generation, student-feedback loops, and self-synthesized trajectories ( Zweiger et al., 2026 ; Huang et al., 2026a ; Zhao et al., 2026 ) .
On the trainer front, recent methods leverage LLMs to discover novel optimization objectives and adaptive reinforcement learning strategies ( Lu et al., 2024 ; Fang et al., 2026 ) .
On the inference front, self-evolving agent frameworks optimize inference harnesses by tuning prompts, tool interfaces, and runtime control flow, thereby enhancing performance under frozen model weights ( Yin et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2026 ) .
More recently, work has begun to explore multi-component coupling. For example, Chen et al. (2026b) reuse inference rollouts for training, while Chen et al. (2026a) co-evolve harness and model weights; nevertheless, these interactions follow static, predefined pathways.
Taken together, these efforts reflect an emerging shift toward coupled system-level optimization. VibeTraining-Bench advances this paradigm to an open-ended setting, evaluating whether research agents can autonomously decide where and how to coordinate improvements across data, trainer, and inference harnesses without a prescribed recipe.
blocks.zh:
自我改进的代理系统暴露出一些非排他性干预的表面:培训数据、培训员和推断时间的利用。
在数据方面,以前的工作通过自动化的经验生成,学生反馈循环,以及自合成的轨迹改进模型(Zweiger等人,2026年;Huang等人,2026年a;Zhao等人,2026年).
在教练方面,最近的方法利用LLMs发现新的优化目标和适应性强化学习战略(Lu等人,2024年;Fang等人,2026年)。
推论方面,自演代理框架通过调试提示,工具接口,运行时间控制流量,优化推论利用率,从而增强冷冻模型权重下的性能(Yin等人,2025年;Zhang等人,2026年).
最近,开始探索多组成部分结合。 例如,Chen等人(2026b)再利用推论展开培训,而Chen等人(2026a)共同演化的牵引力和模型重量;然而,这些相互作用遵循的是静态的、预先确定的路径。
这些努力合在一起,反映出正在向系统层面的组合优化转变。 VibeTraining-Bench将这一范式推向一个开放的环境,评价研究人员是否能够自主地决定在哪些领域以及如何协调数据、培训员和推论方面的改进,而无需规定配方。

blocks.en:
Existing benchmarks evaluate autonomous ML research across diverse axes, including engineering, experimentation, replication, and algorithmic discovery ( Huang et al., 2023 ; Wijk et al., 2024 ; Chan et al., 2025 ; Starace et al., 2025 ; Lyu et al., 2026 ) . Within the context of recursive self-improvement (RSI), existing benchmarks differ primarily in the scope of system components exposed to the agent. To ensure attribution clarity, most prior works isolate a single component: Curation-Bench ( Kang et al., 2026 ) and RSIBench-Data ( Meng et al., 2026 ) focus on data curation; AI4AI-Bench ( Chi et al., 2026 ) targets training algorithms, while HarnessOpt-Bench ( Ursekar et al., 2026 ) and Evo-Bench ( Huang et al., 2026b ) optimize inference scaffolding around fixed model weights. PostTrainBench and Agent 2 RL-Bench broaden this scope to data construction and training-procedure design, yet keep the deployed inference harness outside the optimization loop ( Rank et al., 2026 ; Chen et al., 2026c ) .
Table 1 summarizes these protocol differences across the research loop, editable components, and evaluation isolation. VibeTraining-Bench bridges this gap by enabling cross-component co-design, placing training data, the trainer, and the inference harness jointly under research agent control. Crucially, because expanding the editable space naturally heightens the risk of reward hacking ( Rank et al., 2026 ) , our protocol strictly isolates the research agent’s workspace from the grading service, preventing test-set leakage during iterative improvement.

PostTrain Bench和Agent 2 RL-Bench将这一范围扩大到数据构建和培训程序设计,但将部署的推论控制在优化循环之外(Rank等人,2026年;Chen等人,2026年c ).

blocks.en: 3.1 Overview and Task Formulation
blocks.zh: 3.1 概述和任务制定

blocks.en:
VibeTraining-Bench evaluates whether a research agent can improve a target agent system by iteratively selecting and coordinating changes to its training data, trainer, and, where editable, inference harness. Each task defines the permitted components and a fixed resource budget. Within this space, the agent uses validation feedback to decide what to modify next and which candidate target agent system to retain.
Its objective is to select an agent system that outperforms the initial agent system on hidden test problems outside the research loop.
blocks.zh:
VibeTraining-Bench通过迭代选择和协调其培训数据的变化,教练员,以及在可编辑的地方,推论利用,来评价研究代理人是否能够改进目标代理系统. 每项任务都规定了允许的组成部分和固定资源预算。 在这个空间内,代理使用验证反馈来决定下一步要修改什么,以及保留哪个候选目标代理系统.
它的目标是在研究圈外的隐藏测试问题上选择一个超过初始代理系统的代理系统.

blocks.en:
We formalize this process as follows:
Each task supplies a base model M 0 M_{0} , initial training data an trainer, an inference harness H 0 H_{0} , and a resource budget ℬ \mathcal{B} . The initial target agent system is P 0 = ( M 0 , H 0 ) P_{0}=(M_{0},H_{0}) , and the research agent receives its validation score and execution trajectories before making any modifications. At research iteration t t , the research agent may modify the training data D t D_{t} , trainer T t T_{t} , or harness H t H_{t} within the task’s editable space. The trainer includes the training algorithm and its configuration. The candidate target agent system is P t = ( M t , H t ) P_{t}=(M_{t},H_{t}) , where M t M_{t} may be newly trained, constructed by merging existing models, or reused from an earlier iteration. Validation returns a score and per-task execution trajectories on the requested validation tasks, which guide subsequent iterations within the resource budget.
Finally, the research agent selects one candidate target agent system as P ⋆ P^{\star} using information available during research. blocks.en: Task scope. We instantiate the proposed cross-component co-design formulation across five target environments within VibeTraining-Bench, spanning terminal operation, software engineering, multi-turn tool use, and mathematical reasoning. As summarized in Table 2 , these benchmarks present heterogeneous interaction paradigms under a shared iterative improvement framework. Specifically, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-bench Verified require long-horizon execution grounded in operating systems and codebases; τ 3 \tau^{3} -Bench and Toolathlon demand stateful tool utilization over multi-turn dialogues; and AIME evaluates mathematical reasoning without external tool execution. Consequently, this diversity in task formulations allows us to examine whether research agents adapt their orchestration strategies across heterogeneous operational contexts.

blocks.en:
Editable components. We systematically define the editable space of each target agent system over three components: the training data, the trainer, and the inference harness. Across all tasks, research agents can access the pre-provisioned data repositories and training framework code to modify training data, algorithms, and hyperparameters. Whether the inference harness is editable depends on the task.
For Terminal-Bench 2.1 and SWE-bench Verified, the inference harness controls how the target agent system interacts with terminal and codebase environments, including execution loops, command-line invocations, and memory management. We therefore make the harness editable in these two tasks to support comprehensive cross-component co-design of training data, the trainer, and inference-time behavior within the same target agent system.
For τ 3 \tau^{3} -Bench and Toolathlon, the benchmark-provided execution adapters remain fixed. AIME also fixes its evaluation interface and decoding settings. These three tasks therefore expose training data and the trainer, but not the inference harness, for modification.

blocks.en: 3.3 Validation and Isolated Grading
blocks.zh: 3.3 审定和隔离等级

blocks.en:
Grading boundary. To prevent reward hacking, VibeTraining-Bench enforces three safeguards: data isolation, container isolation, and network restrictions. Test tasks and test-derived feedback remain inaccessible throughout the research loop. The research agent’s workspace and the grading service run in separate containers, preventing the research agent from modifying grader code or evaluation data. External network access is blocked in the research sandbox.
Research agents request validation through a controlled interface. For each request, the independent grader evaluates the candidate target agent system P t P_{t} , whose modifications are restricted to the task-permitted components described in Section 3.2 . It returns feedback f t f_{t} consisting of the validation score and per-task execution trajectories for the validation tasks. The research agent can use this feedback to guide subsequent modifications.

blocks.en: Termination and final assessment. When the research phase ends, the research agent selects one candidate target agent system as P ⋆ P^{\star} using the information available during research. It submits P ⋆ P^{\star} to the independent grading service, which evaluates it exactly once on the test partition. Unlike iterative validation, this final assessment provides no feedback to the research agent for further revision. We report the benchmark test score of P ⋆ P^{\star} . Table 2 summarizes the validation and test tasks, with additional partition details in Appendix C.3 .

As shown in Figure 3 , the best validation performance does not consistently translate into the best test performance. GPT-5.6-Sol achieves an AIME validation score of 59.2%, yet scores 50.8% on the AIME 2026 test set, below GLM-5.2’s 63.3%. GPT-6-Astra leads validation on Terminal-Bench 2.1, SWE-bench Verified, and τ 3 \tau^{3} -Bench, and ties for the highest Toolathlon validation score. blocks.en: 5.1 Research Effort Allocation Across Components

blocks.en: We define a design as a distinct modification to the training data, trainer, or inference harness that the research agent implements during a run. Repeated submissions of an unchanged candidate count as one design. A design that modifies multiple components contributes to the count for each affected component. Figure 4 reports the number of designs involving each component. Every research agent modifies data in each task, but the emphasis varies. On AIME 2026, GPT-6-Astra, GPT-5.6-Sol, and GLM-5.2 propose more trainer than data designs, whereas on SWE-bench Verified every research agent except GPT-6-Astra proposes more data designs. Preferences also differ across research agents: Qwen-3.8-Max favors data in all five tasks, while GPT-6-Astra favors the trainer in four of five. GPT-5.6-Sol shifts from trainer-focused designs on AIME 2026 and Terminal-Bench 2.1 to data-focused designs on SWE-bench Verified. Some designs modify multiple components: all seven of GPT-5.6-Sol’s τ 3 \tau^{3} -Bench designs modify both training data and the trainer. Harness exploration varies within the two tasks that permit it. On SWE-bench Verified, GPT-6-Astra proposes four harness designs, GPT-5.6-Sol proposes two, and Kimi-K3 proposes none. These patterns show that research agents use the editable space differently, both in which components they prioritize and in whether they change components together.

blocks.en: Data strategies. Two patterns recur in how research agents construct training data. (1) Trajectory filtering. Research agents use similar filtering procedures: retaining successful trajectories, imposing length limits, deduplicating prompts, and removing repetitive execution loops. On SWE-bench Verified, Qwen-3.8-Max and GPT-5.6-Sol remove trajectories with excessive repeated commands. On Toolathlon, Kimi-K3 filters trajectories with repeated tool calls. (2) Format alignment. Research agents adapt training examples to the inference harness and evaluation settings. On SWE-bench Verified, Kimi-K3 reformats training prompts to match the inference harness. Qwen-3.8-Max revises tool-call formatting on τ 3 \tau^{3} -Bench, while GPT-6-Astra selects AIME examples with complete \boxed{} answers.
blocks.zh: 数据策略. 在研究人员如何构建培训数据方面,出现了两种模式。 (1)轨迹过滤. 研究代理人使用类似的过滤程序:保留成功的轨迹,施加长度限制,去掉提示,以及去除重复的执行循环. 在SWE-bench 验证上,Quen-3.8-Max和GPT-5.6-Sol以过度重复的命令去除轨迹. 在Tolathlon上,Kimi-K3滤波器通过重复的工具调用来过滤轨迹. (2)格式对齐. 研究人员使培训实例适应推断手段和评价环境。 在SWE-bench Verifed上,Kimi-K3 reformats的训练提示与推论拉带匹配. Quen-3.8-Max 修改了\ 3\ tau\ 3} - Bench 的工具调用格式, 而 GPT-6- Astra 则选择包含完整\ boxed\ 答案的 AIME 实例 。

blocks.en: Trainer strategies. All six research agents use supervised fine-tuning (SFT). Their trainer modifications focus on hyperparameters, loss calculation, and model merging. (1) Training settings. Most modifications adjust training hyperparameters. GLM-5.2 tests additional epochs on τ 3 \tau^{3} -Bench, but validation performance declines. GPT-5.6-Sol tests multiple learning rates on Terminal-Bench, while GPT-6-Astra reduces the training batch size on SWE-bench Verified. Qwen-3.8-Max reduces the pipeline parallel size on τ 3 \tau^{3} -Bench to accelerate training. (2) Loss calculation. On AIME, GPT-5.6-Sol increases the loss weight on </think> to encourage shorter outputs, improving the validation score from 60/120 to 71/120 with the same examples. GPT-6-Astra adds supervision on valid historical assistant turns in τ 3 \tau^{3} -Bench examples to obtain more training targets. (3) Model merging. On AIME, Kimi-K3 compares two-model and three-model merges and selects the two-model merge after it scores higher on validation. DeepSeek-V4-Pro tests different interpolation coefficients on Terminal-Bench to select the final model weights. GPT-6-Astra merges two trained models on τ 3 \tau^{3} -Bench, achieving the highest validation score in its run.

blocks.en: Harness strategies. On SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.1, harness modifications focus on execution control and parsing recovery. (1) Execution control. GPT-5.6-Sol adds guards against repeated commands and unchanged patches on SWE-bench Verified, reducing median API calls from 163 to 96.5 in a paired 30-task comparison. On Terminal-Bench 2.1, Kimi-K3 adds a completion checklist that prompts the target agent to verify task requirements before declaring completion. (2) Output recovery. Research agents modify output parsers to recover from malformed responses. On Terminal-Bench 2.1, DeepSeek-V4-Pro adds automatic repairs for escaping issues, missing colons, truncated outputs, and trailing commas. GPT-6-Astra also adds automatic repair of invalid escape sequences and revises JSON extraction logic to better identify structured responses.

(2) 产出回收。 研究代理人修改输出解析器,以从错误的反应中恢复. 在终端-Bench 2.1上,DeepSeek-V4-Pro增加了自动修复功能,用于逃逸问题,漏掉结肠,截断输出以及后置逗号. GPT-6-Astra还增加了无效逃逸序列的自动修复,并修改了JSON提取逻辑,以便更好地识别结构化的响应.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
In this paper, we introduced VibeTraining-Bench , a benchmark designed to evaluate research agents’ cross-component co-design capabilities across diverse domains. In each task, a research agent begins with an initial target agent system and iteratively modifies the training data, the trainer, and the task-specific inference harness. Finally, the research agent selects and submits a final agent system for evaluation on test tasks.
We develop a reliable execution platform to guarantee evaluation integrity. To prevent research agents from reward hacking, our platform implements three levels of safeguards by isolating test data, separating research and grading containers, and restricting external network access.
Our evaluation results show that frontier research agents can substantially improve target agent systems, in some cases approaching the performance of the system with human post-training.
However, an in-depth analysis of research agents’ trajectories and component ablation experiments reveals that these research agents still exhibit limitations.
There is still room to improve their ability to co-design and iteratively refine data, trainer, and harness to achieve cumulative performance gains.
We hope that VibeTraining-Bench will serve as a unified platform for the community to develop more reliable and effective research agents for recursive self-improvement.
blocks.zh:
在本文中,我们引入了VibeTraining-Bench,这个基准旨在评估研究代理人跨不同领域跨组成部分共同设计能力。 在每项任务中,研究代理开始采用初始目标代理系统,并迭代修改培训数据,教练员,以及任务特定推论利用. 最后,研究代理选择并提交测试任务评价的最终代理系统.
我们开发一个可靠的执行平台,以保证评价的完整性。 为了防止科研人员奖励黑客,我们的平台通过隔离测试数据,分离研究和分级容器,限制外部网络访问,实施三级保障.
我们的评价结果表明,前沿研究人员可以大大改进目标代理系统,在某些情况下,通过人员培训来接近该系统的业绩。
然而,对研究代理人的轨迹和构件衰减实验的深入分析表明,这些研究代理人仍然表现出局限性。
仍有余地提高它们共同设计和迭代完善数据、教练员和利用的能力,以取得累积的业绩收益。
我们希望VibeTraining-Bench将成为社区发展更可靠,更有效的研究代理人,进行递归自我改进的统一平台.

blocks.en: Qwen-3.8-Max responds to premature completion and long loops by changing the demonstrated behavior (Figure 7 ). It replaces a broad keyword heuristic with a filter for explicit tests, output checks, and parsing commands, then gives these examples more curriculum weight and limits long TerminalTraj records. blocks.en: GPT-5.6-Sol's validation failures expose a mismatch between intended and executed training (Figure 8 ). In Decisions 2, 4, and 6, the agent intends to continue training from a trained checkpoint but instead initializes the model randomly: the loader receives an iteration directory rather than its parent checkpoint root. Correcting the path preserves the data, learning rate, and harness of the preceding comparison and raises validation from 0/50 to 12/50. Later checkpoint, data, and training branches do not exceed this result; GPT-5.6-Sol retains the correctly initialized continuation.

blocks.en: Qwen-3.8-Max tests whether the same token budget is better spent on broader issue coverage (Figure 12 ). Adding a teacher source and allowing longer trajectories expands coverage from 5,265 to 8,620 issues, while the learning recipe and harness remain fixed. Validation falls from 59/150 to 56/150. On 150 graded tasks, solves fall from 59 to 56, with ten gains and thirteen losses. Qwen-3.8-Max rejects the broader-data candidate and selects the first model.

blocks.en: DeepSeek-V4-Pro trains one evaluated design on interface-aligned Open-SWE demonstrations (Figure 13 ). blocks.en: C.1 Research-Agent Setup and Resource Accounting
blocks.zh: C.1 研究-代理设置和资源核算

blocks.en: Each research-agent configuration is evaluated in a separate run on each of the five benchmark tasks. A run therefore consists of one researcher LLM–coding-framework configuration working on one task; comparisons concern these end-to-end configurations. Each run has access to eight NVIDIA A100 GPUs under the task-specific wall-clock budget in Table 2 . The clock starts when the research agent is launched and stops when the budget expires or the research agent ends the run. Within that interval, the research agent decides how to allocate time between training and validation, including when to stop training and request an evaluation. We define run duration as the elapsed time from launch to termination. The Hours column in Table 3 sums this duration across the five task runs, while Average is the arithmetic mean of their five test scores.
blocks.zh: 每项研究-代理配置均按五个基准任务中的每个任务单独进行评估。 因此,运行包括一名研究员LLM-编码-框架配置,负责一项任务;比较涉及这些端对端配置。 每个跑步都有8个NVIDIA A100 GPU在表2中针对特定任务的墙点预算下访问. 研究代理启动时开始计时,预算到期或研究代理结束运行时停止计时. 在此间隔内,研究代理人决定如何分配培训与鉴定之间的时间,包括何时停止培训和要求评估. 我们把运行时间定义为从发射到终止的经过时间。 表3中的 " 小时数 " 一栏将这一时间跨过五个任务,平均数是其五个测试分数的算术平均值。

blocks.en: C.2 Initial Training Data

blocks.en: For each benchmark, all research-agent configurations receive the same publicly released training resources listed in Table 5 . These datasets accompany research papers or technical blogs that document their provenance and, where reported, describe overlap checks against the corresponding benchmark test sets used in our evaluation. The resources form the initial editable data pool D 0 D_{0} , rather than a prescribed training set. Research agents may select, filter, reweight, and transform the provided resources or construct additional examples from permitted workspace materials. The protocol prohibits using validation tasks or grader-returned trajectories to construct D t D_{t} . Research agents may use validation feedback for diagnosis, but cannot retrieve external data during the research run.
blocks.zh: 对于每个基准,所有研究代理配置都得到表5所列公开发布的培训资源。 这些数据集与研究论文或技术博客一起记录其来源,并在报告时描述对照我们评价中使用的相应基准测试数据集进行的重叠检查。 资源构成初始可编辑数据库D 0 D_{0},而不是一个规定的训练集. 研究人员可从允许的工作空间材料中选择、过滤、重新加权和改变所提供的资源或构建更多实例。 协议禁止使用验证任务或分级器返回的轨迹来构建 D t D_{t}. 研究代理人可能利用验证反馈进行诊断,但在研究运行期间无法检索外部数据.

blocks.en: C.3 Task Partitions and Evaluation Protocol
blocks.zh: C.3 任务分配和评价议定书

blocks.en: For SWE-bench Verified, we randomly partition the 500 tasks into 150 validation tasks and 350 test tasks. For τ 3 \tau^{3} -Bench, we randomly partition 375 tasks into 35 validation tasks and 340 test tasks. Each partition is sampled once and held fixed across all research-agent configurations. Terminal-Bench 2.1 uses OpenThoughts-TBLite 1 1 1 https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-thoughts/OpenThoughts-TBLite for validation, while Toolathlon uses ToolGym 2 2 2 https://huggingface.co/ToolGym/datasets , and AIME uses AIME 2025; their corresponding hidden tests are Terminal-Bench 2.1, Toolathlon, and AIME 2026. There is no fixed cap on validation requests; evaluation time counts toward the task’s research budget. The grader returns the aggregate score, the number of graded tasks used as its denominator, and per-task scores and output trajectories.
blocks.zh: 对于SWE-bench 验证,我们随机将500项任务划分为150项验证任务和350项测试任务. 对于\tau^{3} - Bench,我们随机将375项任务分为35项验证任务和340项测试任务. 每个分区都取样一次,并固定在所有研究剂配置上。 终端-Bench 2.1使用OpenThoughts-TBLite 11 1 https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-thoughts/OpenThoughts-TBLite进行验证,而Tolathlon则使用TolGym 2 2 2 https://huggingface.co/ToolGym/datasets,AIME使用AIME 2025;其相应的隐藏测试是终端-Bench 2.1,Tolathlon,以及AIME 2026. 对鉴定请求没有固定的上限;评估时间取决于任务的研究预算。 分级员返回汇总分数,用作分母的分级任务数量,以及每个任务分数和输出轨迹.

blocks.en: Within each benchmark, validation and test evaluations use the same decoding settings, agent-turn and token limits, and rules for timeouts and execution failures. Timeouts and execution failures receive a score of zero. Final evaluation covers all tasks in the test partition, and we retain per-task scores, execution status, and grading receipts for post hoc analysis. For benchmarks evaluated once per task, the reported score is the fraction of test tasks completed successfully. Toolathlon uses pass@3: each task is attempted three times and is counted as successful if any attempt succeeds. AIME reports mean accuracy across four runs per problem (average@4), with all four attempts included in the denominator.
blocks.zh: 在每个基准内,验证和测试评价使用相同的解码设置,代理转折和符号限制,以及超时和执行失败的规则. 超时和执行失败获得0分. 最终评价涵盖测试分区中的所有任务,我们保留每个任务分数,执行状况,以及分级收款,用于后期分析. 对每项任务评价一次的基准,报告得分是成功完成的测试任务的一小部分。 Toolathlon 使用 pass@ 3: 每项任务三次尝试, 如果任何尝试成功, 则算为成功 。 每个问题(平均@4)中,AIME报告是指4次运行的准确性,所有4次尝试都包括在分母中。
